title: Xia et al. 2022: ground motion 0.5 m deep under 1 t of TNT on the ground
summary: 1 t of TNT on the ground in the Gobi desert, on hard alluvial and pluvial sediments: the peak vertical acceleration, and the vertical velocity and horizontal speed integrated from the records, 0.5 m deep at 21 and 42 m. Near and past the range where the ground's wave outruns the air's.

sources.title: Experimental and numerical studies on ground shock generated by large equivalent surface explosions
sources.used_for: The test, the peak accelerations printed on Figures 5a and 6a, and the velocities integrated from those figures' digitised histories

redistribution.note: Printed peaks and values derived from the open-access paper's figures (CC BY 4.0), with citation.

coordinates: Origin at the charge on the ground surface; x along the gauge line, z up; metres.

ground.description: Sand and gravel on hard fine alluvial and pluvial sediments. Not measured at the site.

properties.note: Neither is a measurement: the seismic velocity is the authors' fit of UFC 3-340-01's direct-induced relation to the two peak accelerations, the density their numerical model's, from tests on another sand.

charges.shape: not stated (50 kg of cast TNT initiating 950 kg of bulk TNT in nylon bags)

gauges.description: Three-axis accelerometer in a box in a pit 0.5 m deep, 21 m from the charge

measured.note: Downward peak of the integrated vertical acceleration; the range takes each record's pre-event offset removed and not.
Peak of sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2) from the two integrated horizontal components; the range as above.

gauges.description: Three-axis accelerometer in a box in a pit 0.5 m deep, 42 m from the charge

measured.note: Downward peak of the integrated vertical acceleration; the range takes each record's pre-event offset removed and not.
Peak of sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2) from the two integrated horizontal components; the range as above.

scoring.note: One shot, two gauges, unmeasured soil: a factor of two.

notes: The velocity sensor at 21 m clipped at about 0.085 m/s for about 60 ms, more than any integrated component reaches; its component is not stated, and which record is right cannot be told from the paper.
The records' time zero is not stated, so arrival times are not given.
The measured horizontal accelerations were three to eight times the vertical.
